key_insight: This paper proposes an on-board AI pipeline that detects marine anomalies directly on Earth observation satellites, reducing the need to downlink all raw sensor data. By combining self-supervised learning with multi- or hyperspectral imagery, it aims to spot events like oil spills, algal blooms, and sediment floods earlier and more efficiently.
problem_solved: Marine hazards are costly and time-sensitive, but traditional monitoring relies on large-volume satellite data transmission and post-processing on the ground. The paper addresses the challenge of detecting environmental anomalies quickly and efficiently, especially when onboard compute and communication are limited.
method: Uses a self-supervised neural network to learn normal marine spectral patterns from satellite imagery.
Performs anomaly detection onboard the satellite using multi- or hyperspectral sensor data.
Flags unusual observations for prioritized transmission or further analysis, improving bandwidth and response efficiency.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows how compact, self-supervised models can enable real-world edge deployment in resource-constrained remote sensing systems. It is especially relevant for building scalable monitoring pipelines where early detection and low-latency decisions matter.

paper_title: On-Board Anomaly Detection for Efficient Marine Environmental Monitoring
paper_authors: Thomas Goudemant, Clotilde Szywala, Benjamin Francesconi, Michelle Aubrun, Yves Bobichon
